requested_changes.body:
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `for dir in data/*` loop is not robust. If the `data/` directory is empty, the glob `data/*` will be treated as a literal string, causing the commands within the loop to fail as they expect a directory path. 

Additionally, variables containing file paths like `$dir` should be quoted to handle names with spaces or special characters correctly. This is a general shell scripting best practice.

I recommend adding a check to ensure that `$dir` is a directory before processing it and quoting its usage. This will make the script more robust.

Here is a suggested implementation:
```bash
for dir in data/*; do
    if [ -d "$dir" ]; then
        utils/fix_data_dir.sh --utt_extra_files "orthography" "$dir"
        utils/validate_data_dir.sh --non-print --no-feats "$dir" || exit 1
        # make empty files for not-yet generated extra texts
        touch "$dir/text.prev" "$dir/text.ctc"
    fi
done
```
